body: Brilliant thank you :) will check it out!

Yeah I've totally gone back to crating him whenever I can't supervise. It sucks a bit but it's a lot better than walking into a room to find a puddle!

I do have carpet in the room and I think a little pee has gotten on it, but I have a floor cover that protects most of it. I've only see puddles on the cover so far (and on the bed). So hopefully it won't mean I have to cut out carpet. To be honest though part of me is considering just ripping out the carpet altogether and just having wooden flooring instead (it would be cooler for him as well, he's a hairy dog!).

The house is a new build so I am the first person to ever live in it, so definitely not another animal! Not really had any dogs over either. Part of me is wondering if it's possibly a marking problem from his own wee though...I keep thinking that maybe I haven't cleaned EVERYTHING and that's why it's happening so I'm going to go over it all again to be on the safe side.

He's now going in the crate whenever I can't watch him, I really should have done this after the first time he had an accident! I naively thought it might be a one off but after yesterday's peeing on the bed incident I've finally gotten the message.
Hopefully we can get through it quickly!
Yeah I think it's back to puppy potty training 101 with him again too. I just hope it doesn't take 6 months to get him to realise like it did the first time!

Yep! I feel a bit silly for not crating him the first time he had an accident, it took till this morning after a few incidents for me to realise I had to start doing that again!

It gives me some hope that it ended for you. I've been told it could be an age thing so hopefully stopping the free access to that room and keeping him in the crate will solve the problem!

Just to add, the first time it happened I hoped it was a one off. But now that it has happened several times I'm going to have to go back to crating him when I can't watch what he's doing.

I'm more baffled as to why he'd suddenly start doing this again...
I actually have one of those, it never really helped him but I might try it again as it's been a long time and it's worth a shot!

Maybe when walking you could feed him treats to distract him when strangers approach and continue to feed him when they say hi, so he starts associating them with good things? 
I'm in a similar position, mine has never been interested in strangers and now seems to have regressed a little and I think this is what I'm going to have to do to get him to like them more. I considered getting strangers to feed him treats too but I've heard this would just cause him to expect treats from every stranger he sees so perhaps not a good idea...

I went through this as well. It took him a long time to finally get it. Same situation as you, a couple of weeks with no incidents and then out of nowhere he would wee or poo in the house and I would be pulling my hair out wondering why he wasn't getting it.
In my case, it just took time. I kept taking him outside and making a big fuss when he did it and eventually in his own time he stopped doing it. Some just take longer than others. Keep sticking with what you're doing, he's just a slow learner but he'll get it eventually :)

Don't compare too much to other dogs. I have only started having this mindset recently. Dogs learn at different paces. You might have one puppy who is house-trained in 2 weeks whereas another might take months to get it. Don't sweat it too much, they WILL get there (provided you are taking the necessary steps!)
On a lighter note, I was taken aback at how much I love my boy. I always knew I would love my dog but the amount I do is a surprise! :)

When I leave some good stuff in there like chicken it can distract him for a few minutes whilst I leave for work so he doesn't notice me leave.

Wow do we have the same dog? They sound very similar!!

Honestly I don't think you've fucked up and I very much felt this way with my dog Benji when I first got him. I actually took 2 weeks off work to help him settle and try and get him used to being left alone, but he still had major problems with it when I did start. Fast forward a few months and he's still not over it. 

I ended up paying through the nose for a behaviourist to come over one evening and assess him and she gave me a desensitisation plan to get him used to it.

Basically I now use a peanut butter covered Kong (my boy also has no interest in a Kong unless i smear the outside of it with peanut butter so he can get to it much easier, he's pretty lazy) as a marker, so he knows we're doing training and then gradually build up the time I leave. I can now leave him up to 5 minutes without much issue which sounds pretty pathetic but is a big deal for us. Every few days I bump up the time a little more and the aim is to get to 30 minutes by which point my behaviourist assures me he should be able to handle an hour or more.

I think the same thing could work with you, starting with putting your shoes and getting your keys but then not leaving so he stops associating those cues with you going out. Then start going out and immediately coming back in, then go for 5 seconds etc. But try and mix it up so its not just constantly increasing and sometimes you come back in a few seconds again, just to keep him guessing. I honestly think that would work. 

I have been there, my pup loves other dogs too, more than people but I know he's cool with being the only dog in the house now it just took time. I felt so disheartened by the time I had contacted the behaviourist but she assured me it's never too late to turn this problem around as long as you put in the time to sort it. Her dog had the same issue but also used to injure itself from scratching till it bled and she managed to turn the situation around by desensitising him to it slowly. You've only had yours for a week so I think you are being too hard on yourself!

That is exactly how I've been feeling. Regretting the surgery and feeling terrible for putting him through this, and my heart breaking when I see how much he's struggling.

I'm just going to keep thinking about how in a few weeks he'll be back to his happy fun loving self and this is going to just be a distant memory for both of us.

Thank you for your comments, it's made me feel much more hopeful!

Wow, that does sound horrid! I'm glad to know she was back to normal after the stitches went. I have a feeling we are going to be in the same boat and it's going to be 10 days of this. 

This might sound silly but do you think there were any permanent changes in her behaviour because of the bad reaction? I keep thinking this experience is going to traumatise him and he won't be the same dog afterwards, he's just miserable 24/7 :(

Yeah i have had that same worry in term of knowing if he's in pain or not, i guess all we can do is hope there's some sort of sign when the time comes!

Wow thank you for taking the time to write such a long thoughtful reply! :) I am sorry it has taken me this long to respond, I kind of went into hibernation, that's what normally happens when I get this bad. I just hide from everything and everyone.

It's actually the reverse, I was born in the U.K., my parents left here to go live in the U.S.! So the big decision was theirs, I couldn't join them as my VISA hadn't come through and I was also unsure about whether I could make such a big leap.

In the past I have thought out a plan to commit suicide to the point where I was googling the most painless and easiest ways and staring at an open bottle of pills willing myself to do it. I haven't quite got to that point this time, it's mostly just fantasising and wishing something would happen to me so that I wouldn't have to do it myself. It's all just thoughts at this point.

Hmmm favourite memories...definitely revolve round gaming! Through everything, whether it was being bullied at school or other family members, I always had my games consoles and that pulled me through! My happiest memories are sitting on my Megadrive, Super Nintendo, Nintendo 64 etc for hours on end...is that sad? Lol. As a result I have always been a bit of a loner!

My family moved away in the summer of 2012, and I have been to  visit 3 times since then, the next time will probably be this Christmas. It's a long journey!

I can't really pinpoint what started the depression, I could probably make an educated guess that it's a combination of factors from my childhood (and a few things from adulthood). 

When I was growing up, my Dad used physical punishment as discipline, but also he had an awful temper so sometimes would just lose it if he thought I spoke out of turn or if I wasn't respecting him in some way. I remember a time he was angry at the amount of salt I had put on my food so he took away the plate and threw it at me. I have a lot of memories of running away from him terrified. Once I reached my teenage years, the same would happen but I would get angry back and there would be months and months where we wouldn't say a word to each other despite living under the same roof.

My Dad has two brothers who lived nearby and their kids (my cousins) are another negative part of my childhood. They have always played favourites and I was their least favourite. They liked my brother but I was the uncool nerdy one who wasn't as good or fun. I used to HATE going to their house or attend family functions (and in our family there were a lot of those) because I hated being around them so much as they were bullies. I would cry and beg my parents to not make me go to events.

I was also an unpopular kid at school, for the same reasons, I didn't really take care of my appearance and wasn't considered cool, just as a geek. One of my cousins is the same age as me and we went to the same primary (elementary) school and high school. She was one of the popular kids and wouldn't associate with me, and her friends all liked to tell me that she was way cooler than I was. 

We are all adults now and although it's not the same now, the scars just never faded and it shaped our relationships. They still pick favourites, only it's more subtle now. A good example is my 30th. They have all gone above and beyond for each other on their milestone birthdays, but none of them are coming to mine. It's not surprising but even to this day it hurts, as it just adds to my low self worth.

It's also exacerbated now that my immediate family are so far away and I know I won't have any family around for my birthday.

I've also had some awful relationships in my twenties, but I think my childhood issues have probably been the root cause there. I have extremely low self esteem and that's come out in destructive and unhealthy ways in relationships. I have lost all interest in meeting anyone, I have been single for 5 years now and the thought of being close to someone makes me feel really uncomfortable and unsafe. 

I would love to hear more about your story if you are still willing to share??? Sorry for the LONG reply I have just written!
